title: Garden and Oath
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Rosalind Vasquez's forbidden gift for speaking with beasts becomes the only way to navigate a country that is literally forgetting itself—villages, roads, and people fading from memory as the long winter falls. Guided by a scarred mountain cat named Bracken and pursued by the Wardens who once trained her mother, Rosalind joins a ragtag found family of smugglers, exiles, and one amnesiac Warden to seek the Last Door, the ancient exit out of Thornfell's dying borders. Along the way she learns her gift is an inheritance: her mother sealed the Door shut to trap something hungry beneath the mountains. In the end, Rosalind must choose between reopening the Door to save her companions or renewing her mother's oath—and she finds a third path, binding the hunger with shared memory rather than sacrifice, so that Thornfell's survivors walk out into a starlit world carrying their country inside them.
about_author: S. M. Voss is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six winters leading mule trains through remote mountain passes and swears half her stories were told to her by the animals. She writes fantasy about stubborn women, talkative beasts, and the places we carry when home disappears.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Smuggling contraband honey through a hidden pass, she notices the stars flicker and die while the border wards hum and snap like cut harp strings. Her mule refuses to go home. The chapter ends with her racing toward Thornfell village as the first snow falls—snow that does not melt. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine shattered.

chapters.title: A Village That Forgets Its Own Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Back in Thornfell, she finds the innkeeper has forgotten his daughter's face, and the village well remembers water it never held. Only Rosalind's beast-speaker gift lets her hear how frightened the animals are. She meets Tam, a smuggler friend, and agrees to guide him north—for pay, she insists. Beat: loneliness cracking open into reluctant connection.

chapters.title: Bracken
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A scarred mountain cat speaks to her in full sentences—the first beast ever to do so—warning that 'the Door is leaking.' He claims to have known her mother. Rosalind, whose gift has always been a secret shame, is shaken that a wild thing knows her family. Beat: wonder tangled with grief for the mother she barely remembers.

chapters.title: The Warden Without a Past
chapters.summary: Warden Elias's POV. A Warden wakes on the frozen road with no memory except his oath and his orders: find the Vasquez girl. He rescues a fading child from a village being erased and begins to doubt which side of his orders serves mercy. Beat: duty at war with dawning conscience; introduces the antagonist institution sympathetically.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Remember
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Following Bracken to a cave of hibernating bears, Rosalind learns beasts hold memories humans lose—her mother's voice among them, singing a sealing song. The bears show her a vision of the Last Door beneath Mount Cael. Beat: inheritance revealed; Rosalind stops running from her gift and starts asking what it's for.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At a smugglers' waystation she gathers her found family: Tam the fence, old Marta who maps roads that no longer exist, and Pip, a boy erased from everyone's memory but his own. They argue about whether to flee south or seek the Door. Rosalind chooses the Door. Beat: the family forms around a shared impossible purpose.

chapters.title: Wards and Wardens
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias tracks the group but hesitates at the waystation, finding Marta's maps familiar—he may have grown up here before the Order took him. His superior, High Warden Corvane, arrives and demonstrates the Order's true aim: not saving Thornfell, but harvesting its stored memory before it dies. Beat: Elias's faith fractures.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Marta leads them down a road only she remembers, which exists just long enough as they walk it. Pip nearly fades when he doubts himself; Rosalind anchors him by telling his story back to him until the snow releases him. Beat: the theme lands—memory kept alive is memory shared aloud.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Corvane corners them at a shrine, offering Rosalind safety and training if she surrenders her gift to the Order's harvest. Bracken attacks; they escape through a collapsing pass, but Tam takes a wound that won't heal in the forgetting cold. Beat: the enemy's seductive logic stated plainly; cost of defiance made real.

chapters.title: Tam's Long Sleep
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Sheltering in a shepherd's bothy, Tam fades in and out, forgetting Rosalind between lucid hours. She keeps him present by recounting every job they ever ran together. Elias appears unarmed, offering Warden medicine, and Rosalind must decide whether to trust him. Beat: trust extended across enemy lines; tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Oath My Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias recovers fragments of memory: he was the novice assigned to watch Rosalind's mother, and he loved her platonically, like a sister. He reveals she didn't seal the Door to imprison the hunger—she sealed it to buy time for someone with a stronger gift to be born. Beat: Elias chooses Rosalind over the Order; guilt transmuted into loyalty.

chapters.title: Crows on the Col
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Corvane's crows—beasts twisted into memory-eaters—ambush the party on a high col. Rosalind speaks to them and discovers they're terrified, hollowed things that remember being ordinary birds. She frees two; the rest scatter. Pip saves her life. Beat: compassion as weapon; the found family fights as one for the first time.

chapters.title: Marta's Map of Everything
chapters.summary: Marta's POV (first non-Rosalind chapter). Dying of age and erasure, Marta gives Rosalind her life's map—every road, grave, and name of Thornfell inked from memory—and asks Rosalind to speak it back to her so she can die whole. Rosalind does, weeping. Beat: the book's heart; inheritance passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Beneath Mount Cael
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They descend through dwarven ruins where carved names still glow faintly. Bracken confesses he was her mother's companion, bound to guard the Door until a Vasquez returned. The hunger below whispers to each of them in the voices of those they've lost. Beat: descent into the past; temptation personalized.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They reach the Door: a seam of starlight in living rock, the last piece of the vanished sky. Opening it would release the trapped hunger along with everyone else. Corvane arrives with harvested memories bottled in glass, demanding Rosalind open it so the Order can drain the country cleanly. Beat: all forces converge; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Corvane Lost
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Corvane and learns the High Warden lost his own family to an earlier forgetting and believes controlled harvest is mercy—that nothing should be allowed to simply end. Their duel is fought more with arguments than blades. Elias wins by refusing to kill him. Beat: the antagonist humanized; violence refused without victory feeling cheap.

chapters.title: The Hunger Speaks
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The hunger offers Rosalind her mother's full memory, her village restored, everything—if she opens the Door. She almost does. Bracken steps between her and the light, offering his own nine lives instead. Rosalind realizes the hunger isn't evil; it's a country's fear of being forgotten, gone ravenous. Beat: climax of temptation; insight over force.

chapters.title: A New Oath
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Instead of opening or resealing the Door, Rosalind leads everyone—survivors, freed crows, even broken Corvane—in speaking Thornfell's memories aloud into the seam: Marta's map, Tam's stories, Pip's name, her mother's song. The hunger feeds on shared telling rather than stolen memory and quiets. Beat: climax resolved through the book's central idea—memory held together.

chapters.title: Walking Out
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Door opens gently onto a spring morning under returning stars. The refugees step through carrying seeds, Marta's map, and the mountain cat. Behind them, Thornfell sleeps under clean snow, no longer dying but dreaming. Tam wakes fully healed. Beat: exhale after climax; bittersweet leaving of home.

chapters.title: The Naming
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. In the valley beyond, the refugees build a first camp. Pip, once erased, is asked to name the new settlement and chooses 'Thornfell,' insisting countries live in people, not borders. Elias plants his Warden badge in the earth and walks away from the Order. Beat: resolution through renewal; the next generation inherits deliberately.

chapters.title: Letters to a Sleeping Country
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Seasons pass. Rosalind teaches refugee children to listen to beasts, and Bracken naps in the schoolhouse sun. She writes letters she leaves at the closed seam each solstice, telling the sleeping land its own stories so it never wakes hungry again. Beat: quiet epilogue; ritual replacing fear.

chapters.title: Garden and Oath
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Years later, Rosalind returns through the Door one last time and finds Thornfell waking—a green country remembering itself, her mother's voice in the wind finishing the sealing song as a welcome rather than a warning. She plants a garden at the Door's threshold and renews the oath in her own words. Final beat: inheritance fulfilled, home redefined, stars overhead.
